title: Research: kernel-check guarded Compact repair under explicit completion premises
body:
PR2378 explicitly leaves the actual Compact extraction/key/reinsertion algorithm outside its completed-primitive theorem. This adds a Lean4.34.1/Std proof of that repair stage's successful-completion endpoint: arbitrary payloads are returned at their ideal inverse addresses, assuming the stated raw inverse/good-set laws and successful destination/exhaustion guards.

The proof follows unchanged PR2250 source: extract `(ideal(rawInverse(q)), payload)`, preserve whole key/payload pairs through the stable binary passes, and consume them at matching marked holes. Pair preservation is proved; sortedness and total completion remain open. This is a local formal module, not a discharged `CompletedPrimitive`, physical cost theorem, supplier, or new kappa.

Validation:

- Fresh pinned Lean4.34.1 kernel build: four named roots; only `propext` and `Quot.sound`; four actual false propositions rejected; axiom-output negative control.
- Source-authenticated complete layouts: 10,240 tagged addresses across an earlier-source all-exception case and a mixed good/exception constant case; original repair, full primitive and second invocation checked; ten semantic/control cases.
- Registered Python3.12 normal/optimized replay and Git-free read-only export with seven corruption/CLI controls.
- Separate Codex agent read the proof/source and independently replayed Python3.12.7 and the fresh Lean harness with no blocker.

From the repository root:

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/compact-repair-guarded-refinement
python3.12 -I -O -B research/compact-repair-guarded-refinement/kernel.py --lean /absolute/path/to/lean.exe
```

The second command requires official Windows x86_64 Lean4.34.1 commit5045d0056413266e57c625dcd7c365b10e377c52. Installed compiler/Std binaries remain trusted. Python receipt validation is explicitly not a fresh kernel run. The Python-to-Lean source translation, all-size raw laws, guard success, tape restoration/cost and consumer toolchain bridge remain external obligations. Guidance revision5 milestone: narrow and stop at the local formal handoff until those obligations have a named consumer and plan.

Credit: Jose Manuel/jmbarrancoml for PR2250 source and proof; AAAmirinu for PR2378's consumer and explicit handoff; Gareth Davidson/bitplane, Douglas Colkitt and DreamingOfClouds for the credited foundations. Original bytes/notices and exact commit/blob/SHA256 pins are retained. Prepared under ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including independent AI review; no human or maintainer acceptance is implied.
